explicit_semantics.new_attempt_initiation_allowed: true ONLY for blocked_not_executed (the gate-level / no-active-attempt pre-initiation condition): an explicit coordinator action may create a fresh attempt ONLY when no attempt is active. false for launch_committed, ok, execution_failed.
explicit_semantics.current_attempt_model_load_allowed: true ONLY for launch_committed (the already-created attempt may proceed to its model loader, under the supervised-launch protocol). false for blocked_not_executed (no attempt created), ok, execution_failed.
explicit_semantics.launch_committed_meaning: launch_committed means ONLY that the already-created attempt may proceed to its model loader under the supervised-launch protocol (parent holds the OS-backed inter-process lock; the worker cannot reach a model loader before the durable launch_committed event + startup barrier are established; the worker MUST NOT write lifecycle registry events). It MUST NOT authorize creation/initiation of another attempt.
explicit_semantics.new_attempt_after_terminal: Terminal records never transition or get rewritten. After an attempt is terminal, a later attempt is created as a NEW record with a NEW attempt_id through a separate explicit coordinator initiation, never via a transition from the terminal record, and only after the previous attempt has a terminal lifecycle event.
explicit_semantics.terminal_ok_meaning: terminal ok means ONLY that the supervised worker completed successfully and the supervisor structurally captured the expected per-attempt evidence pair (hashes). It does NOT mean independently verified, canonical, deployment-suitable, or compatibility-frozen.
explicit_semantics.canonical_selection_and_freeze_are_post_: canonical_selected and compatibility_frozen are append-only non-lifecycle annotation events in the same single authoritative registry; they never rewrite a terminal event.

forbidden_patterns: rewriting a prior attempt's durable record
treating a later attempt as a retry of a failed attempt ID
initiating a new attempt while any attempt is active or launch_committed
creating or initiating another attempt under launch_committed (launch_committed authorizes only the already-created attempt to proceed to its model loader)
transitioning from a terminal record into a new attempt (a later attempt is a NEW record with a NEW attempt_id via a separate explicit coordinator initiation)
placing the runtime attempt registry inside an attempt output root that can be atomically replaced or rejected as pre-existing by the live publisher
a worker subprocess writing lifecycle registry events
automatic retry or an automatic recovery loop that launches a new attempt after a dangling launch_committed
appending canonical_selected without an independent verifier validating a terminal ok
appending compatibility_frozen without a prior canonical_selected and a separately authorized compatibility-freeze action
rewriting or augmenting a terminal ok event with canonical/freeze status
attempt_contract.later_attempt_definition: A later attempt is a NEW explicit attempt with a NEW immutable attempt_id, never a retry or continuation of a failed attempt_id, and never a transition from a terminal record; it may be initiated only after the previous attempt has a terminal lifecycle event. The three timed inference passes inside one attempt are MEASUREMENT REPETITIONS within that same attempt, not retries.

supervised_launch_protocol.parent_role: external bounded supervisory parent: holds the OS-backed inter-process exclusive lock from pre-launch check through the terminal lifecycle event; spawns and supervises the worker; appends ALL lifecycle registry events; observes worker exit/timeout/interruption/crash and appends exactly one terminal event; terminates the worker on bounded timeout; sanitizes failure details; the worker MUST NOT write lifecycle registry events.
supervised_launch_protocol.worker_role: child worker subprocess: performs the model load + inference + measurement; MUST NOT write any lifecycle registry event; can only reach a model loader after the durable launch_committed event and the lock protocol are established (startup barrier).
supervised_launch_protocol.startup_barrier: a parent/worker startup barrier (or equivalent) so the worker cannot reach a model loader before the durable launch_committed event and the lock protocol are established.

lock.scope: OS-backed inter-process exclusive lock; held from pre-launch check through the terminal lifecycle event; SIBLING path outside any attempt output directory; enforces at most one attempt in launch_committed (non-concurrent).

worker_started_event.when: appended by the parent after launch but before the startup barrier opens; records worker identity/liveness.
worker_started_event.kind: permitted non-terminal lifecycle metadata event; it does not grant any lifecycle transition.

dangling_launch_reconciliation.condition: a process killed/crashed after the durable launch_committed event but before any terminal event leaves a dangling launch_committed.
dangling_launch_reconciliation.policy: NEVER automatic retry and NEVER an automatic recovery loop that launches a new attempt.
dangling_launch_reconciliation.explicit_coordinator_action: an explicit coordinator reconciliation action acquires the same OS-backed inter-process lock, positively confirms the worker is not alive (or the startup barrier cannot proceed), then appends exactly one execution_failed terminal event with a truthful result_reason (e.g. dangling_launch_reconciled).
dangling_launch_reconciliation.liveness_unestablishable: if liveness cannot be established, the reconciliation BLOCKS and does NOT start another attempt.
dangling_launch_reconciliation.allowed_because: this terminal append is allowed because launch_committed is NON-terminal; no terminal event is ever rewritten.
dangling_launch_reconciliation.later_attempt: a later attempt is only a NEW separately initiated attempt_id after the previous attempt has a terminal lifecycle event; reconciliation does not launch a new attempt.

blocked_not_executed.description: Initial (gate-level) state for every attempt. No attempt record exists, no worker exists, and no model loader has begun. This is the no-active-attempt pre-initiation condition: an explicit coordinator action MAY create a fresh attempt ONLY when no attempt is active.

launch_committed.description: The coordinator has explicitly initiated THIS attempt via the supervised-launch protocol: the supervising parent holds the OS-backed inter-process exclusive lock (verification/phase16-raw-corpus-entity-layer/.raner_smoke_attempt_registry.lock), assigned a fresh immutable attempt_id, and durably recorded it (append-only launch_committed event in the authoritative SIBLING runtime registry, verification/phase16-raw-corpus-entity-layer/raner_smoke_attempt_registry.jsonl) BEFORE the worker can reach any model loader (startup barrier). The worker may proceed to its model loader only after the durable launch event and lock protocol are established; the worker MUST NOT write lifecycle registry events. launch_committed means ONLY that the already-created attempt may proceed to its model loader under supervision. It MUST NOT authorize creation/initiation of another attempt. At most one attempt may be launch_committed (non-concurrent). A dangling launch_committed (worker killed/crashed before any terminal event) is terminalized ONLY by explicit coordinator reconciliation (append exactly one execution_failed; never automatic retry).

ok.description: Terminal success for this attempt in the lifecycle sense ONLY: the supervised worker completed successfully and the supervisor structurally captured the expected per-attempt evidence pair (hashes). It does NOT mean independently verified, canonical, deployment-suitable, or compatibility-frozen. Cannot transition to any other state and is never rewritten. Post-terminal canonical_selected / compatibility_frozen annotation events are separate append-only records.

execution_failed.description: Terminal failure for this attempt (supervisor-observed outcome: timeout, interruption, crash, runtime_error, launch_denied, supervisor_observed_exit; or explicit coordinator reconciliation of a dangling launch: dangling_launch_reconciled). Permanently retained with its immutable attempt_id and result_reason. Cannot transition to any other state and is never retried, reused, or rewritten.

transitions.trigger: Coordinator explicitly and separately initiates a new attempt: the supervising parent acquires the OS-backed inter-process exclusive lock, assigns a fresh immutable attempt_id, and durably appends the launch_committed event to the authoritative SIBLING runtime registry BEFORE the worker can reach any model loader (startup barrier). Requires NO active attempt (no attempt launch_committed or non-terminal) and no prior use of the same attempt_id. After an attempt is terminal, a later attempt is created as a NEW record with a NEW attempt_id through a separate explicit coordinator initiation, never by a transition from the terminal record, and only after the previous attempt has a terminal lifecycle event.

The supervising parent observes the worker exit successfully and structurally captures the expected per-attempt evidence pair (hashes); it appends exactly one ok terminal event. ok means supervised completion ONLY (not independent verification, not canonical, not compatibility-frozen). Later canonical_selected / compatibility_frozen are separate post-terminal annotation events.

The supervising parent observes worker failure, timeout, interruption, crash, or launch denial and appends exactly one execution_failed terminal event (sanitized failure details; worker terminated on bounded timeout); OR an explicit coordinator reconciliation terminalizes a dangling launch_committed by appending exactly one execution_failed with a truthful reason (blocks if liveness cannot be established; never automatic retry / no recovery loop). The record becomes terminal for that attempt and is permanently retained.

invariants: No transition out of a terminal state; terminal records are never transitioned or rewritten.

After an attempt is terminal, a later attempt is created as a NEW record with a NEW attempt_id through a separate explicit coordinator initiation, never via a transition from the terminal record, and only after the previous attempt has a terminal lifecycle event.

launch_committed is durably recorded by the supervising parent as an append-only event in the authoritative SIBLING runtime registry BEFORE the worker can reach a model loader (startup barrier); there is exactly one launch_committed event per attempt_id and no second launch event for the same ID.

Exactly one terminal event (ok or execution_failed) per attempt_id; no terminal rewrite; failed history is permanently retained. Terminal events are appended by the supervising parent or the explicit coordinator reconciliation - never by the worker.
The worker subprocess MUST NOT write lifecycle registry events.
The supervising parent holds the OS-backed inter-process exclusive lock from pre-launch check through the terminal lifecycle event; at most one attempt may be active/launch_committed.
launch_committed allows ONLY the already-created attempt to proceed to its model loader under supervision; it never authorizes creation/initiation of another attempt.

A dangling launch_committed is terminalized ONLY by explicit coordinator reconciliation (acquire the same lock, confirm the worker is not alive / the startup barrier cannot proceed, append exactly one execution_failed); if liveness cannot be established, block and do not start another attempt; never automatic retry / no recovery loop.
Timeout, interruption, and crash are terminal failure outcomes of an attempt (as result_reason under execution_failed); they are not states and never allow model loading.
terminal ok means supervised completion + supervisor-captured evidence-pair hashes ONLY; it is NOT independent verification, canonical, deployment-suitable, or compatibility-frozen.

canonical_selected and compatibility_frozen are post-terminal append-only annotation events (zero-or-one per current Phase 16); they never rewrite a terminal event; supersession requires a separately authorized planning amendment.
A failed attempt is permanently retained and its attempt_id is never retried or reused.
A later attempt is a new explicit attempt, never a retry of a failed attempt_id.
The three timed inference passes inside one attempt are measurement repetitions within that attempt, not retries.
